dedupe_keys.name: singapore four national taps water resilience story centre for liveable cities pub

description: This case study, told by the chairman of PUB, Singapore's national water agency, explains how an island city-state of over five million people on 718 square kilometres, ranked 170th of 193 countries for natural water resources in the 2006 UN World Water Development Report, built a resilient supply. It records droughts in 1960 and 1963 to 1964 that forced rationing, dry spells in 2010 and 2014, and the driest February in 145 years with 0.2 millimetres of rain. The response was a strategy from the 1972 Water Master Plan of four national taps: local catchment water held in 17 reservoirs, imported water, NEWater reclaimed water introduced in 2003, and desalination from 2005 with plants of 136,000 and 318,500 cubic metres per day, plus demand management through pricing and efficiency standards. Coverage: one country, 1960s to 2015, narrative with some quantities, not a dataset. Access: a free PDF; the licence is not stated. Caveats: an agency-authored account of its own success, with limited cost data. It informs supply diversification, drought resilience and capacity planning models, and relates to the Orange County groundwater replenishment case study on potable reuse in the catalogue.
